nodes.name: self-similar set (attractor) of an iterated function system
nodes.statement: The self-similar set (the attractor) given by the system of contracting similarities $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ (iterated function system) of a complete metric space is the unique compact set $T$ satisfying $T=\cup_{i=1}^n f_i(T)$.
differentia: given by the system of contracting similarities $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ (iterated function system) of a complete metric space
satisfying $T=\cup_{i=1}^n f_i(T)$

nodes.name: shift on the space $\xo$ / on the space $\xmo$
nodes.statement: The \textit{shift on the space $\xo$} is the map $\sigma:\xo\rightarrow\xo$, which deletes the first letter of a word, i.e. $\sigma(x_1x_2x_3\ldots) = x_2x_3\ldots$. The \textit{shift on the space $\xmo$} is the map also denoted by $\sigma$, which deletes the last letter of a word, i.e. $\sigma(\ldots x_3x_2x_1) = \ldots x_3x_2$. The shifts are continuous $|X|$\,-\,to\,-$1$ maps. The branches $\sigma_x$ for $x\in X$ of the inverse of $\sigma$ are defined by $\sigma_x(x_1x_2\ldots)=xx_1x_2\ldots$ and $\sigma_x(\ldots x_2x_1)=\ldots x_2x_1x$.
nodes.statement_short: The one-sided shifts $\sigma$ on $\xo$ and $\xmo$ delete the first, resp. last, letter, with inverse branches $\sigma_x$.
nodes.origin_citation: standard symbolic dynamics; cf. Lind & Marcus 1995
nodes.definiendum: shift on the space $\xo$ / on the space $\xmo$
differentia: which deletes the first letter of a word
which deletes the last letter of a word

nodes.name: Bernoulli measure $\mu_p$
nodes.statement: Let $p=(p_x)_{x\in X}$ be a probability vector (fixed for the rest of the section) and let $\mu_p$ be the \textit{Bernoulli measure} on $\xo$ with weight $p$, i.e. this measure is defined on cylindrical sets by \[ \mu_p(x_1x_2\ldots x_n\xo)=p_{x_1}p_{x_2}\ldots p_{x_n}. \] The measure on $\xmo$ is defined in the same way.
differentia: defined on cylindrical sets by $\mu_p(x_1x_2\ldots x_n\xo)=p_{x_1}p_{x_2}\ldots p_{x_n}$

nodes.name: uniform Bernoulli measure $\mu_u$ and the one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift
nodes.statement: In case $p_x=\frac{1}{|X|}$ for all $x\in X$, the measure $\mu_p$ is the \textit{uniform Bernoulli measure} denoted $\mu_u$. The dynamical system $(\xo,\sigma,\mu_u)$ is called the \textit{one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift}. The measure $\mu_p$ is the unique regular Borel probability measure on $\xo$ that satisfies the self-similarity condition: \[ \mu_p(A)=\sum_{x\in X} p_x\mu_p(\sigma_x^{-1}(A)) \] for any Borel set $A\subset\xo$.
nodes.statement_short: The equal-weight Bernoulli measure $\mu_u$; $(\xo,\sigma,\mu_u)$ is the one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift, and $\mu_p$ is the unique self-similar Borel probability measure.
differentia: $p_x=\frac{1}{|X|}$ for all $x\in X$

nodes.name: a sequence starts / ends in a vertex; the set $V(w)$
nodes.statement: Let $\gr=(V,E)$ be such a graph and take a vertex $v\in V$. We say that a sequence $x_1x_2\ldots\in\xo$ (a word $x_1x_2\ldots x_n\in X^{*}$) \textit{starts in the vertex $v$} if there exists a right-infinite path $e_1e_2\ldots$ (finite path $e_1e_2\ldots e_n$) in $\gr$, which starts in $v$ and is labeled by $x_1x_2\ldots$ (respectively $x_1x_2\ldots x_n$). Similarly, we say that a sequence $\ldots x_2x_1\in\xmo$ (a word $x_n\ldots x_2x_1\in X^{*}$) \textit{ends in the vertex $v$} if there exists a left-infinite path $\ldots e_2e_1$ (finite path $e_n\ldots e_2e_1$) in $\gr$, which ends in $v$ and is labeled by $\ldots x_2x_1$ (respectively $x_n\ldots x_2x_1$). For every $w\in X^*\cup\xmo$ denote by $V_\gr(w)=V(w)\subset V$ the set of all vertices $v\in V$ such that the sequence $w$ ends in $v$. Observe that $V(w'w)\subseteq V(w)$ for arbitrary word $w'$ and finite word~$w$.
nodes.statement_short: A sequence starts (ends) in $v$ if some infinite path from (to) $v$ carries it as label; $V(w)$ collects all vertices in which $w$ ends.
nodes.definiendum: starts in the vertex $v$ / ends in the vertex $v$; $V_\gr(w)=V(w)$
differentia: such that the sequence $w$ ends in $v$

nodes.name: the sets $B_v$, $F_v$ and the sofic subshifts $\B$, $\F$
nodes.statement: For every vertex $v\in V$ denote by $B_v$ the set of all right-infinite sequences that start in $v$, and denote by $F_v$ the set of all left-infinite sequences that end in $v$. The sets $B_v$ and $F_v$ are closed correspondingly in $\xo$ and $\xmo$, thus compact and measurable. The sets $\B=\cup_{v\in V}B_v$ and $\F=\cup_{v\in V}F_v$ are the one-sided (respectively, right and left) \textit{sofic subshifts} associated with the graph $\gr$. The sets $F_v, v\in V$, satisfy the recursion \[ F_v=\bigcup_{u\, \stackrel{x}{\rightarrow} \,v} \sigma_x(F_u) \] (here the union is taken over all edges which end in $v$). Hence, associating the map $\sigma_x$ with every edge $e$ of the graph $\gr$ labeled by $x$, the collection of sets $\{F_v, v\in V\}$ can be seen as the graph-directed iterated function system on the sofic subshift $\F$ with the underlying graph $\gr$ (see \cite{fractal_gr_sets}). All the maps $\sigma_x^{-1}$ are restrictions of the shift $\sigma$, and thus $\{F_vx, v\in V\}$ is the Markov partition of the dynamical system $(\F,\sigma)$. Similarly, the collection of sets $\{B_v, v\in V\}$ can be seen as the graph-directed iterated function system on the sofic subshift~$\B$.
nodes.statement_short: $B_v$ / $F_v$ are the right- / left-infinite sequences starting / ending in $v$; their unions are the sofic subshifts and form a graph-directed IFS.
differentia: all right-infinite sequences that start in $v$
all left-infinite sequences that end in $v$

nodes.name: right-resolving and strictly right-resolving labeled graph
nodes.statement: A labeled graph $\gr=(V,E)$ is called \textit{right-resolving} (Shannon graph in some terminology) if for every vertex $v\in V$ the edges starting at $v$ have different labels. Every sofic subshift can be given by a right-resolving graph (see Theorem~3.3.2 in \cite{IntroSymbDyn}). A right-resolving graph is called \textit{strictly right-resolving} if every vertex $v\in V$ has an outgoing edge labeled by $x$ for every $x\in X$.
differentia: for every vertex $v\in V$ the edges starting at $v$ have different labels
every vertex $v\in V$ has an outgoing edge labeled by $x$ for every $x\in X$

nodes.name: the vectors $\vec\mu_p(\B)$, $\vec\mu_p(\F)$ and the number $\mu_p(\gr)$
nodes.statement: For a labeled graph $\gr=(V,E)$ we use the following notations: \[ \vec\mu_p(\B)=(\mu_p(B_v))_{v\in V}, \quad \vec\mu_p(\F)=(\mu_p(F_v))_{v\in V}, \quad \mbox{ and } \quad \mu_p(\gr)=\sum_{v\in V} \mu_p(F_v). \]

nodes.name: measure number $\mgr(\gr)$ of a graph
nodes.statement: The number $\mgr(\gr)=\mu_p(\gr)$ is called the \textit{measure number} of the graph~$\gr$.
differentia: $\mgr(\gr)=\mu_p(\gr)$

nodes.name: adjacency matrix $A$ and transition matrix $T_p$ of a labeled graph
nodes.statement: The matrix $A=(a_{vu})_{v,u\in V}$, where $a_{vu}$ is equal to the number of edges from $v$ to $u$, is the \textit{adjacency matrix} of the graph $\gr$. For the probability vector $p=(p_x)_{x\in X}$ define the matrix \[ T_p=(t_{vu})_{v,u\in V}, \mbox{ where } t_{vu}=\sum\limits_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u}p_x \] (the sum is taken over all edges from $v$ to $u$). The matrices $A$ and $T_p$ are irreducible if and only if the graph $\gr$ is strongly connected. If the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving, then the matrix $T_p$ is the \textit{transition matrix} of the random walk on the weighted directed graph $\gr$, where each edge labeled by $x$ has weight $p_x$. In this case the row sums of the matrix $A$ are $\leq |X|$, and the row sums of the matrix $T_p$ are $\leq 1$, hence the spectral radius of $A$ is $\leq |X|$, and the spectral radius of $T_p$ is $\leq 1$. If the graph $\gr$ is strictly right-resolving, then the transition matrix $T_p$ is right stochastic.
nodes.statement_short: $A$ counts edges; $T_p$ weights each edge $v\to u$ by $p_x$, and is the transition matrix of the $p$-weighted random walk on a right-resolving $\gr$.
nodes.origin_citation: standard nonnegative-matrix theory; cf. Lind & Marcus 1995
differentia: $a_{vu}$ is equal to the number of edges from $v$ to $u$
$t_{vu}=\sum\limits_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u}p_x$

nodes.name: self-similar action and the restriction $g|_x$
nodes.statement: A faithful action of a group $G$ on the set $X^*$ is called \emph{self-similar} if for every $g\in G$ and $x\in X$ there exist $h\in G$ and $y\in X$ such that \[ g(xw)=yh(w) \] for all $w\in X^*$. The element $h$ is called the \textit{restriction} of $g$ on $x$ and denoted $h=g|_x$. Inductively one defines the restriction $g|_{x_1x_2\ldots x_n}=g|_{x_1}|_{x_2}\ldots |_{x_n}$ for every word $x_1\ldots x_n\in X^n$. Notice that $(g\cdot h)|_v=g|_{h(v)}\cdot h|_v$ (we are using left actions).
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.genus: faithful action of a group $G$ on the set $X^*$
differentia: for every $g\in G$ and $x\in X$ there exist $h\in G$ and $y\in X$ such that $g(xw)=yh(w)$ for all $w\in X^*$

nodes.name: virtual endomorphism; the action defined by a triple $(\phi,T,C)$
nodes.statement: The study of the self-similar actions of a group is in some sense the study of the \textit{virtual endomorphisms} of this group, which are homomorphisms from a subgroup of finite index to the group. There is a general way to construct a self-similar representation of a group with a given associated virtual endomorphism. Let $\phi: H\rightarrow G$ be a virtual endomorphism of the group $G$, where $H<G$ is a subgroup of index $d$. Let us choose a left coset transversal $T=\{g_0,g_1,\ldots,g_{d-1}\}$ for the subgroup $H$, and a sequence $C=\{h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_{d-1}\}$ of elements of $G$ called a \emph{cocycle}. The self-similar action $(G,X^{*})$ with the alphabet $X=\{x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1}\}$ defined by the triple $(\phi,T,C)$ is given by \[ g(x_i)=x_j,\qquad g|_{x_i}=h_j^{-1}\phi(g_j^{-1}gg_i)h_i, \] where $j$ is such that $g_j^{-1}gg_i\in H$ (such $j$ is unique). The action may be not faithful, the kernel can be described using Proposition~2.7.5 in \cite{self_sim_groups}.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.statement_short: A virtual endomorphism is a homomorphism from a finite-index subgroup; together with a coset transversal $T$ and cocycle $C$ it determines a self-similar action.
nodes.definiendum: virtual endomorphism; cocycle; action defined by the triple $(\phi,T,C)$
nodes.genus: homomorphisms from a subgroup of finite index to the group
differentia: $\phi: H\rightarrow G$ where $H<G$ is a subgroup of index $d$

nodes.name: contracting self-similar action, nucleus $\nucl$, Moore diagram
nodes.statement:
An important class of self-similar actions are contracting actions. A self-similar action of a group $G$ is called \emph{contracting} if there exists a finite set $
ucl$ such that for every $g\in G$ there exists $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $g|_v\in
ucl$ for all words $v\in X^*$ of length $\geq k$. The smallest set $
ucl$ with this property is called the \emph{nucleus} of the self-similar action. The nucleus itself is self-similar in the sense that $g|_v\in
ucl$ for every $g\in
ucl$ and $v\in X^{*}$. It can be represented by the 	extit{Moore diagram}, which is the directed labeled graph with the set of vertices $
ucl$, where there is an edge from $g$ to $g|_x$ labeled $(x,g(x))$ for every $x\in X$ and $g\in
ucl$. We identify the nucleus with its Moore diagram, also denoted by $
ucl$. The contracting property of the action depends only on the virtual endomorphism but not on the chosen coset transversal and cocycle (see Corollary~2.11.7 in \cite{self_sim_groups}). Notice that every contracting self-similar group is countable.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.statement_short: An action is contracting if all deep restrictions land in a finite set; the minimal such set is the nucleus, encoded by its Moore diagram.
nodes.definiendum: contracting self-similar action; nucleus; Moore diagram
differentia: there exists a finite set $\nucl$ such that for every $g\in G$ there exists $k\in\mathbb{N}$ such that $g|_v\in\nucl$ for all words $v\in X^*$ of length $\geq k$

nodes.name: asymptotic equivalence on $\xmo\times G$
nodes.statement: Let us fix a contracting self-similar action $(G,X^{*})$. Consider the space $\xmo\times G$ of all sequences \ $\ldots x_2x_1\cdot g$, $x_i\in X$ and $g\in G$, with the product topology of discrete sets $X$ and $G$. Two elements $\ldots x_2x_1\cdot g$ and $\ldots y_2y_1\cdot h$ of $\xmo\times G$ are called \textit{asymptotically equivalent} if there exist a finite set $K\subset G$ and a sequence $g_n\in K, n\geq 1,$ such that \begin{displaymath} g_n(x_n x_{n-1}\ldots x_1)=y_n y_{n-1}\ldots y_1\qquad \mbox{ and }\qquad g_n|_{x_n x_{n-1}\ldots x_1}\cdot g=h \end{displaymath} for every $n\geq 1$. This equivalence relation can be recovered from the nucleus $\nucl$ of the action (Proposition~3.2.6 in \cite{self_sim_groups}).
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.statement_short: Two points of $\xmo\times G$ are asymptotically equivalent when a bounded sequence of group elements matches their prefixes at every level.
nodes.genus: equivalence relation on elements of $\xmo\times G$
differentia: there exist a finite set $K\subset G$ and a sequence $g_n\in K, n\geq 1,$ such that $g_n(x_n x_{n-1}\ldots x_1)=y_n y_{n-1}\ldots y_1$ and $g_n|_{x_n x_{n-1}\ldots x_1}\cdot g=h$ for every $n\geq 1$

nodes.name: limit $G$-space $\limGs$
nodes.statement: The quotient of the set $\xmo\times G$ by the asymptotic equivalence relation is called the \textit{limit $G$-space} of the action and denoted $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$. The group $G$ naturally acts on the space $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$ by multiplication from the right.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
differentia: by the asymptotic equivalence relation

nodes.name: the maps $\tau_x$ on the limit $G$-space
nodes.statement: The map $\tau_x$ defined by the formula \[ \tau_x(\ldots x_2 x_1\cdot g)=\ldots x_2 x_1 g(x)\cdot g|_x \] is a well-defined continuous map on the limit $G$-space $\limGs$ for every $x\in X$, which is not a homeomorphism in general. Inductively one defines $\tau_{x_1x_2\ldots x_n}=\tau_{x_n}\circ\tau_{x_{n-1}}\circ\ldots\circ\tau_{x_1}$.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.genus: well-defined continuous map on the limit $G$-space $\limGs$
differentia: $\tau_x(\ldots x_2 x_1\cdot g)=\ldots x_2 x_1 g(x)\cdot g|_x$

nodes.name: (digit) tile $\tile$ and the tiles $\tile_v$
nodes.statement: The image of $\xmo\times 1$ in $\limGs$ is called the \textit{(digit) tile} $\tile$ of the action. The image of $\xmo v\times 1$ for $v\in X^n$ is called the \textit{tile} $\tile_v$, equivalently $\tile_v=\tau_v(\tile)$. It follows directly from definition that \[ \limGs=\bigcup_{g\in G} \tile\cdot g \ \ \ \ \mbox{ and } \ \ \ \ \tile=\bigcup_{v\in X^n} \tile_v. \]
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
differentia: the image of $\xmo v\times 1$ for $v\in X^n$

nodes.name: open set condition for a contracting action
nodes.statement:
Two tiles $	ile\cdot g$ and $	ile\cdot h$ intersect if and only if $gh^{-1}\in
ucl$. A contracting action $(G,X^*)$ satisfies the \emph{open set condition} if for any element $g$ of the nucleus $
ucl$ there exists a word $v\in X^*$ such that $g|_v=1$, i.e. in the nucleus $
ucl$ there is a path from any vertex to the trivial state. If the action satisfies the open set condition then the tile $	ile$ is the closure of its interior, and any two different tiles have disjoint interiors; otherwise every tile $	ile\cdot g$ is covered by the other tiles (see Proposition~3.3.7 in \cite{self_sim_groups}).
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.statement_short: The action satisfies the open set condition when every nucleus element has a trivial restriction, equivalently the nucleus has a path from any vertex to $1$.
differentia: for any element $g$ of the nucleus $\nucl$ there exists a word $v\in X^*$ such that $g|_v=1$

nodes.name: limit space $\lims$
nodes.statement: The factor of the limit $G$-space $\limGs$ by the action of the group $G$ is called the \textit{limit space} $\lims=\lims(\phi)$. It follows from the definition that we may also consider $\lims$ as a factor of $\xmo$ by the following equivalence relation: two left-infinite sequences $\ldots x_2 x_1,\ldots y_2 y_1$ are equivalent if and only if there exists a left-infinite path $\ldots e_2 e_1$ in the nucleus $\nucl$ such that the edge $e_i$ is labeled by $(x_i,y_i)$. The limit space $\lims$ is compact, metrizable, finite-dimensional space. It is connected if the group $G$ is finitely generated and acts transitively on $X^n$ for all $n$.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
differentia: by the action of the group $G$

nodes.name: limit dynamical system $(\lims,\si)$
nodes.statement: The equivalence relation on $\xmo$ is invariant under the shift $\sigma$, therefore $\sigma$ induces a continuous surjective map $\si:\lims\rightarrow\lims$, and every point of $\lims$ has at most $|X|$ preimages under $\si$. The dynamical system $(\lims,\si)$ is called the \textit{limit dynamical system} of the self-similar action.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
differentia: $\si:\lims\rightarrow\lims$ is the continuous surjective map induced by the shift $\sigma$

nodes.name: tile $\T_v$ of the $n$-th level in the limit space
nodes.statement: The image of $\xmo v$ for $v\in X^{n}$ in $\lims$ is called the \textit{tile} $\T_v$ of the $n$-th level. Clearly \[ \T_v=\bigcup_{x\in X}\T_{xv}\qquad\mbox{ and }\qquad \si(\T_{vx})=\T_v \] for every $v\in X^{*}$ and $x\in X$. Two tiles $\T_v$ and $\T_u$ of the same level have nonempty intersection if and only if there exists $h\in\nucl$ such that $h(v)=u$. Under the open set condition, every tile $\T_v$ is the closure of its interior, and any two different tiles of the same level have disjoint interiors (Proposition~3.6.5 in \cite{self_sim_groups}).
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.genus: image of $\xmo v$ for $v\in X^{n}$ in $\lims$

nodes.name: limit solenoid $\sol$
nodes.statement: The inverse limit of the topological spaces $\lims\stackrel{\si}{\leftarrow} \lims \stackrel{\si}{\leftarrow} \cdots$ is called the \textit{limit solenoid} $\sol$. One can consider $\sol$ as a factor of the space $\xz$ of two-sided infinite sequences by the equivalence relation, where two sequences $\xi,\eta$ are equivalent if and only if there exist a two-sided infinite path in the nucleus labeled by the pair $(\xi,\eta)$. The two-sided shift on $\xz$ induces a homeomorphism $\e:\sol\rightarrow\sol$.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces

nodes.name: uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphism
nodes.statement: First recall that a measure preserving map with entropy $\log{d}$ is called {\it uniformly $d$-to-one endomorphism} if it is almost everywhere $d$-to-one and the conditional expectation of each preimage is $1/d$. The standard example is $(\xmo,\sigma,\mu_u)$, which is uniformly $|X|$-to-one.

nodes.name: generating function (in the sense of tree-adapted factors)
nodes.statement: Recall the definition of tree very weak Bernoulli and generating function. Let $(Y,S,\mu)$ be uniformly $d$-to-one and $f:Y\rightarrow{R}$ be a tree adapted function to a compact metric space $R$ with metric $D$. The function $f$ is called \textit{generating} if the $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$ is generated by $S^{-i}f^{-1}(\mathcal{B}),i\geq{0}$, where $\mathcal{B}$ is the $\sigma$-algebra of Borel sets of the space $R$.
differentia: the $\sigma$-algebra on $Y$ is generated by $S^{-i}f^{-1}(\mathcal{B}),i\geq{0}$

nodes.name: tree very weak Bernoulli
nodes.statement: Informally, ``tree very weak Bernoulli'' means that for almost all pairs of points in $Y$ their trees of preimages are close. To give a formal definition note that since $S$ is uniformly $d$-to-one, for almost all points $y\in Y$ the set $S^{-k}(y)$ contains exactly $d^k$ points, i.e. the tree of preimages is a $d$-regular rooted tree. The set $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ of finite words over $\{1,\ldots,d\}$ can be considered as a $d$-regular rooted tree, where every word $v$ is connected with $vx$ for $x\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and the root is the empty word $\emptyset$. We can use the tree $\{1,\ldots, d\}^{*}$ to label the trees of preimages. For almost all points $y\in Y$ there is a map $T_y:\{1,\dots,d\}^*\rightarrow{Y}$ such that $T_y(\emptyset)=y$ and $T_y(\sigma(v))=S(T_y(v))$ for all nonempty words $v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Every map $T_y$ is tree adapted, and it is uniquely defined up to an automorphism of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Then $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are called {\it tree very weak Bernoulli} if for any $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a set $W=W(\varepsilon,n)\subset Y$ with $\mu(W)>1-\varepsilon$ such that for any $y,y'\in{W}$ \begin{equation} t_n(y,y')=\min_\psi \frac{1}{n}\sum_{v\in \{1,\dots,d\}^{*}, |v|\leq n}d^{-|v|}D(f(T_y(v)),f(T_{y'}(\psi(v))))<\varepsilon, \end{equation} where the minimum is taken over all automorphisms $\psi$ of the tree $\{1,\dots,d\}^*$. Notice that the definition of $t_n$ does not depend on the choice of $T_y$.
nodes.statement_short: A uniformly $d$-to-one system with $f$ is tree vwb if, off a small set, the $f$-labelled preimage trees of two points can be matched to within $\varepsilon$ in the $t_n$ metric.
nodes.genus: property of a uniformly $d$-to-one system $(Y,S,\mu)$ together with a function $f$
differentia: for any $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$ there is a set $W=W(\varepsilon,n)\subset Y$ with $\mu(W)>1-\varepsilon$ such that for any $y,y'\in{W}$ $t_n(y,y')<\varepsilon$

nodes.name: (standard) integral self-affine tile $T(A,D)$
nodes.statement: Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ integer expanding matrix, where expanding means that every eigenvalue has modulus $>1$. The lattice $\Z^n$ is invariant under $A$, and we can choose a coset transversal $D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\}$ for $\Z^n/A(\Z^n)$, where $m=|det(A)|$. There exists a unique nonempty compact set $T=T(A,D)\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, called (standard) \textit{integral self-affine tile}, satisfying \[ A(T)=\bigcup_{d\in D} T+d. \] The tile $T$ has positive Lebesgue measure, is the closure of its interior, and the union above is nonoverlapping (the sets have disjoint interiors) \cite{lag_wang:self_affine}. It is well known \cite{lag_wang:int_self_affine_I} that the tile $T$ has integer Lebesgue measure.
nodes.statement_short: For an integer expanding matrix $A$ and digit set $D$, the unique compact $T$ with $A(T)=\cup_{d\in D}(T+d)$; it has integer Lebesgue measure.
differentia: satisfying $A(T)=\bigcup_{d\in D} T+d$

nodes.name: iterated monodromy group $IMG(f)$
nodes.statement: Let $f$ be a sub-hyperbolic rational function and let $\M=\Rs\setminus\overline{P}_f$, where $P_f$ is the post-critical set of $f$. Then $f$ defines a $d$-fold partial self-covering $f: f^{-1}(\M)\rightarrow\M$. Take a base point $t\in\M$ and let $T_t$ be the tree of preimages $f^{-n}(t)$, $n\geq 0$, where every vertex $z\in f^{-n}(t)$ is connected by an edge to $f(z)\in f^{-n+1}(t)$. The fundamental group $\pi_1(\M,t)$ acts by automorphisms on $T_t$ through the monodromy action on every level $f^{-n}(t)$. The quotient of $\pi_1(\M,t)$ by the kernel of its action on $T_t$ is the \textit{iterated monodromy group} $IMG(f)$ of the map $f$.
nodes.statement_short: $IMG(f)$ is $\pi_1(\M,t)$ modulo the kernel of its monodromy action on the preimage tree of a sub-hyperbolic rational map.
differentia: by the kernel of its action on $T_t$

nodes.name: Hutchinson's existence and uniqueness of the self-similar measure
nodes.statement: Given a probability vector $p=(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, Hutchinson \cite{hutch:fract_self_similarity} showed the existence of a unique probability measure $\mu$ supported on $T$ satisfying \begin{equation} \mu(A)=\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i\mu(f_i^{-1}(A)), \mbox{ for any Borel set $A$}, \end{equation} which is called the self-similar measure.

nodes.name: Integrality of the measure of a finite right-resolving graph
nodes.statement: Let $\gr=(V,E)$ be a finite right-resolving graph. Then \[ \mu_p(\gr)=\min_{w\in\xmo} |V(w)|=\min_{w\in X^*} |V(w)|. \] In particular, the measure $\mu_p(\gr)$ is integer.

The only property that was used is that for every word $u\in X^{*}$ the set of all words, which contain $u$ as a subword, has measure $1$. nodes.name: Algorithm to find the vector $\vec\mu_p(\B)$ of a right-resolving graph
nodes.statement: At the same time Proposition~\ref{prop_eigenvect_transition_matr} implies the algorithm to find the vector $\vec\mu_p(\B)$ for a right-resolving graph. Indeed, a left eigenvector of $T_p$ for the eigenvalue $1$ is uniquely defined if we know its entries $\mu_p(B_v)$ for vertices $v$ in the strongly connected components of $\gr$ without outgoing edges. For every such a component $\gr'$, we have $B_v=\xo$ and $\mu_p(B_v)=1$ for every vertex $v\in\gr'$ if the component $\gr'$ is a strictly right-resolving graph, and $\mu_p(B_v)=0$ otherwise. In particular, if the matrix $T_p$ is rational then the values $\mu_p(B_v)$ are rational.

nodes.name: The binary adding machine
nodes.statement: Consider the transformation $a$ of the space $X^{*}$ over the binary alphabet $X=\{0,1\}$ defined recursively by the rule \begin{eqnarray*} a(0w)=1w \quad \mbox{ and }\quad a(1w)=0a(w) \end{eqnarray*} for $w\in X^{*}$. The action of $a$ on the space $X^{*}$ corresponds to addition of one in the binary numeration system, and therefore the transformation $a$ is called the (binary) \textit{adding machine}. Indeed, $a(x_1x_2\ldots x_n)=y_1y_2\ldots y_n$ for $x_i,y_i\in X$ if and only if \[ 1+x_1+2x_2+\ldots +2^{n-1}x_n=y_1+2y_2+\ldots+2^{n-1}y_n \mod 2^{n}. \]

nodes.statement_short: The binary odometer $a$: adding one in binary, given recursively by $a(0w)=1w$, $a(1w)=0a(w)$.

nodes.name: Limit spaces of the adding-machine action of $\Z$
nodes.statement: The group generated by $a$ is the infinite cyclic group, and we have a self-similar action of the group $\Z\cong\langle a\rangle$ on the space $X^{*}$. This action corresponds to the virtual endomorphism $\phi:2\Z\rightarrow\Z$ given by $\phi(m)=m/2$ and the coset transversal $T=\{0,1\}$ (there is no need to specify the cocycle for abelian groups). The nucleus of the action $(\Z,X^{*})$ is shown in Figure~\ref{fig_AddingMachine}. It follows that two sequences in $\xmo\times \Z$ are asymptotically equivalent if and only if they are of the form \[ \ldots 000\cdot a^{n+1} \approx \ldots 111\cdot a^n \quad \mbox{or} \quad \ldots 001w\cdot a^n \approx \ldots 110w\cdot a^n \] for $w\in X^{*}$ and $n\in\Z$. This is the usual identification of binary expansions of real numbers (but written to the left). Hence the map $\Phi$ given by the rule \[ \Phi(\ldots x_2x_1\cdot a^n)=n+\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \frac{x_i}{2^i},\quad x_i\in X \mbox{ and } n\in\Z, \] induces a homeomorphism between the limit $G$-space $\limGs[(\Z,X^{*})]$ and the real line $\mathbb{R}$ with the standard action of $\Z$ by translations. The image of the tile $\tile$ under $\Phi$ is the unit interval $[0,1]$. The limit space $\lims[(\Z,X^{*})]$ is homeomorphic to the unit circle.
nodes.section: 3 Self-similar actions and its limit spaces
nodes.statement_short: For the adding machine, $\limGs[(\Z,X^{*})]\cong\mathbb{R}$ with tile $[0,1]$, and the limit space is the circle.

Then \[ \mu|_{\tile}(A)=\sum_{x\in X} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\tile}(\tau_x^{-1}(A)) \] for any Borel set $A\subset\tile$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Tiles scale by $|X|^{-n}$ per level, same-level tiles overlap in measure zero, and $\mu|_{\tile}$ is self-similar for the IFS $\{\tau_x\}$.

nodes.statement: The measure $\mu(\tile)$ is equal to the measure number $\mgr(\gr_\nucl)$ of the nucleus, in particular it is always integer. Moreover, $\mu(\tile)=1$ if and only if the action satisfies the open set condition.
nodes.statement_short: $\mu(\tile)=\mgr(\gr_\nucl)\in\mathbb{N}$, and equals $1$ exactly under the open set condition.
assumptions: Let us fix a contracting self-similar action $(G,X^*)$.
conclusions: The measure $\mu(\tile)$ is equal to the measure number $\mgr(\gr_\nucl)$ of the nucleus
in particular it is always integer
$\mu(\tile)=1$ if and only if the action satisfies the open set condition

nodes.name: The tile measure is algorithmically computable
nodes.statement: The measure $\mu(\tile)=\mgr(\gr_{\nucl})$ can be found algorithmically using the remarks after Proposition~\ref{prop_eigenvect_transition_matr}.

nodes.name: The covering by tiles is a perfect multiple covering
nodes.statement: Every point $x\in\limGs$ is covered by at least $\mu(\tile)$ tiles. The set $\dot{\limGs}$ of all points $x\in\limGs$, which are covered by exactly $\mu(\tile)$ tiles, is open and dense in $\limGs$, and its complement has measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Every point lies in $\geq\mu(\tile)$ tiles, and almost every point in exactly $\mu(\tile)$.
assumptions: Every point $x\in\limGs$
conclusions: is covered by at least $\mu(\tile)$ tiles
The set $\dot{\limGs}$ of all points $x\in\limGs$, which are covered by exactly $\mu(\tile)$ tiles, is open and dense in $\limGs$, and its complement has measure $0$

nodes.name: The boundary of the tile has measure zero
nodes.statement: Let $\partial\tile$ be the boundary of $\tile$. Then $\mu(\partial\tile)=0$.
assumptions: Let $\partial\tile$ be the boundary of $\tile$
conclusions: $\mu(\partial\tile)=0$

nodes.name: Computing the measure of an intersection of two tiles
nodes.statement:
Two tiles $	ile\cdot g_1$ and $	ile\cdot g_2$ for $g_1,g_2\in G$ have nonempty intersection if and only if $g_1g_2^{-1}\in
ucl$. Let us show how to find the measure of this intersection. By Proposition~ef{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} we have  egin{eqnarray*} \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}((	ile\cdot g_1)\cap (	ile\cdot g_2))= igcup_{{\scriptsize egin{array}{c} h_1,h_2\in
ucl \ g_1g_2^{-1}=h_1h_2^{-1} \end{array}}} (F_{h_1}\cap F_{h_2})\cdot h_1^{-1}g_1, \end{eqnarray*} where the sets $F_g$ are defined using the nucleus $
ucl$. The word problem in contracting self-similar groups is solvable in polynomial time \cite[Proposition~2.13.10]{self_sim_groups} (one can use the program package \cite{AutomGrp}). The measures of intersections $F_{h_1}\cap F_{h_2}$ can be found for example using method described after Corollary~ef{cor_meas_gr_rational}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce $\mu(\tile g_1\cap\tile g_2)$ to measures of pairwise intersections $F_{h_1}\cap F_{h_2}$ over nucleus factorizations of $g_1g_2^{-1}$.

nodes.name: When can one choose an action satisfying the open set condition?
nodes.statement: It is an interesting open question in what cases we can always choose a self-similar action which satisfies the open set condition (see \cite{mult_an_self_sim,lag_wang:haar} for the abelian case and applications to wavelets).

nodes.name: The measure on the limit $G$-space depends only on the virtual endomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $\phi: H\rightarrow G$ be a virtual endomorphism of the group $G$. Let $(G,X^*)$ and $(G,Y^*)$ be the contracting self-similar actions defined respectively by the triples $(\phi,T,C)$ and $(\phi,T',C')$. Then the homeomorphism $\alpha : \limGs[(G,X^*)]\longrightarrow \limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ from Theorem~\ref{theor_limsX hom limsY} preserves measure, i.e. \[ \mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A) \] for any Borel set $A$.
nodes.statement_short: The canonical homeomorphism between limit $G$-spaces of two actions with the same $\phi$ is measure preserving.
assumptions: Let $\phi: H\rightarrow G$ be a virtual endomorphism of the group $G$
Let $(G,X^*)$ and $(G,Y^*)$ be the contracting self-similar actions defined respectively by the triples $(\phi,T,C)$ and $(\phi,T',C')$
for any Borel set $A$
conclusions: the homeomorphism $\alpha : \limGs[(G,X^*)]\longrightarrow \limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ from Theorem~\ref{theor_limsX hom limsY} preserves measure, i.e. $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A)$

nodes.name: Uniformity of the Bernoulli measure is essential
nodes.statement: It is important in the theorem that we take the uniform Bernoulli measure on $\xmo$. The problem is that the homeomorphism $\alpha$ may change the Bernoulli measure with a non-uniform weight to a measure that is not Bernoulli.

nodes.name: The set $\mathcal{U}$ is open, dense, of full measure and asymptotically saturated
nodes.statement: The set $\mathcal{U}$ is open and dense in $\xmo$, and $\mu_p(\mathcal{U})=1$. For each $w\in \mathcal{U}$ there is a beginning of $w$ that belongs to $\mathcal{U}^*$, and $\mathcal{U}=\cup_{w\in\mathcal{U}^*}\xmo w$. The sets $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{U}\times G$ are closed under the asymptotic equivalence relation on $\xmo$ and $\xmo\times G$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{U}$ is open, dense, has measure $1$, is generated by finite words, and is saturated for asymptotic equivalence.
conclusions: The set $\mathcal{U}$ is open and dense in $\xmo$, and $\mu_p(\mathcal{U})=1$
For each $w\in \mathcal{U}$ there is a beginning of $w$ that belongs to $\mathcal{U}^*$, and $\mathcal{U}=\cup_{w\in\mathcal{U}^*}\xmo w$
The sets $\mathcal{U}$ and $\mathcal{U}\times G$ are closed under the asymptotic equivalence relation on $\xmo$ and $\xmo\times G$ respectively

nodes.name: Almost every point of $\lims$ has exactly $|X|$ preimages
nodes.statement: Almost every point of $\lims$ has precisely $|X|$ preimages under~$\si$.
conclusions: Almost every point of $\lims$ has precisely $|X|$ preimages under~$\si$

nodes.name: $\rho$ restricted to $\tile_u$ is a homeomorphism for $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$
nodes.statement: Let $\rho$ be the factor map $\limGs\rightarrow\lims$. Then for any $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$ the restriction $\rho|_{\tile_u}:\tile_u\rightarrow\T_u$ is a homeomorphism, $\rho^{-1}(\T_u)=\sqcup_{g\in G}\tile_u\cdot g$.
assumptions: Let $\rho$ be the factor map $\limGs\rightarrow\lims$
for any $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$
conclusions: the restriction $\rho|_{\tile_u}:\tile_u\rightarrow\T_u$ is a homeomorphism
$\rho^{-1}(\T_u)=\sqcup_{g\in G}\tile_u\cdot g$

nodes.name: The projection $\limGs\rightarrow\lims$ is a covering map up to measure zero
nodes.statement: The projection $\limGs\rightarrow\lims$ is a covering map up to sets of measure zero.
conclusions: The projection $\limGs\rightarrow\lims$ is a covering map up to sets of measure zero

nodes.name: The quotient measure $\mu_{*}$ coincides with $\muls$
nodes.statement: The quotient measure $\mu_{*}$ of the limit $G$-space $(\limGs,\mu)$ coincides with the measure $\muls$ on the limit space $\lims$.
conclusions: The quotient measure $\mu_{*}$ of the limit $G$-space $(\limGs,\mu)$ coincides with the measure $\muls$ on the limit space $\lims$

nodes.name: $(\lims,\muls)$ depends only on the virtual endomorphism
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{theor_measure_limGs_invariant} holds for the limit space $\lims$, i.e. the measure space $(\lims,\muls)$ depends only on the associated virtual endomorphism.
conclusions: the measure space $(\lims,\muls)$ depends only on the associated virtual endomorphism

nodes.name: Measure of the tiles $\T_u$ for $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$
nodes.statement: $\muls(\T_u)=\mu(\tile_u)=\frac{1}{|X|^{|u|}}\mgr(\tile)$ for $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$.
assumptions: for $u\in\mathcal{U}^*$
conclusions: $\muls(\T_u)=\mu(\tile_u)=\frac{1}{|X|^{|u|}}\mgr(\tile)$

nodes.name: The limit dynamical system is conjugate to the one-sided Bernoulli shift
nodes.statement: $(\lims,\si,\muls)$ is conjugate to the one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift.
assumptions: Let us fix a contracting self-similar action $(G,X^*)$.
conclusions: $(\lims,\si,\muls)$ is conjugate to the one-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift

nodes.name: Hoffman-Rudolph criterion for one-sided Bernoullicity
nodes.statement: A uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism $(Y,S,\mu)$ is one-sidedly conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift if and only if there exists a generating function $f$ so that $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are tree very weak Bernoulli.
nodes.statement_short: Bernoullicity of a uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism is equivalent to the tree-very-weak-Bernoulli property for some generating $f$.
assumptions: A uniform $d$-to-one endomorphism $(Y,S,\mu)$
conclusions: is one-sidedly conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift if and only if there exists a generating function $f$ so that $(Y,S,\mu)$ and $f$ are tree very weak Bernoulli

nodes.name: The limit solenoid is conjugate to the two-sided Bernoulli shift
nodes.statement: $(\sol,\e,\muls_\e)$ is conjugate to the two-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift.
conclusions: $(\sol,\e,\muls_\e)$ is conjugate to the two-sided Bernoulli $|X|$-shift

nodes.name: Nilpotent setting: Malcev completion and the homeomorphism $\Phi$
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a finitely generated torsion-free nilpotent group. Let $\phi:H\rightarrow G$ be a contracting surjective virtual endomorphism such that the associated self-similar action is faithful (i.e. $\phi$-core($H$) is trivial in the terminology of \cite{sidki:virt_nilp}). Then $\phi$ is also injective by Theorem~1 in \cite{sidki:virt_nilp}, thus $\phi$ is an isomorphism and we can apply Theorem~6.1.6 from \cite{self_sim_groups}. The group $G$ and its subgroup $H$ are uniform lattices of a simply connected nilpotent Lie group $L$ by Malcev's completion theorem. The isomorphism $\phi:H\rightarrow G$ extends to a contracting automorphism $\phi_L$ of the Lie group $L$. There exists a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Phi:\limGs\rightarrow L$ such that $\phi_L(\Phi(t))=\Phi(\tau_{x_0}(t)\cdot g_0)$ for every $t\in\limGs$ and fixed $x_0\in X$ and $g_0\in G$.
nodes.statement_short: Standing hypotheses identifying $\limGs$ with a simply connected nilpotent Lie group $L$ via a $G$-equivariant $\Phi$.

nodes.name: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ is the right Haar measure on $L$
nodes.statement: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs$ is the (right) Haar measure on the Lie group $L$.
conclusions: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs$ is the (right) Haar measure on the Lie group $L$

nodes.name: Extension to virtually nilpotent groups
nodes.statement: The same observation holds in a more general setting of finitely generated virtually nilpotent groups (or under the conditions of Theorem~6.1.6).

nodes.name: Self-similar action of $\Z^n$ realizing an integral self-affine tile
nodes.statement: The inverse of the matrix $A$ can be considered as the contracting virtual endomorphism $A^{-1}: A(\Z^n)\rightarrow\Z^n$ of the group $\Z^n$, which is actually an isomorphism so that we can apply the previous example of this section. Put $X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$ and let $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$ be the self-similar contracting action defined by the virtual endomorphism $A^{-1}$, the coset transversal $D$, and the trivial cocycle $C=\{1,\ldots,1\}$ (see Section~3). The group $\Z^n$ is the uniform lattice in the Lie group $\mathbb{R}^n$. Hence by Theorem~6.1.6 in \cite{self_sim_groups} (see also Section~6.2 there) there exists a $\Z^n$-equivariant homeomorphism $\Phi:\limGs[\Z^n]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^n$ given by \[ \Phi(\ldots x_{i_2} x_{i_1}\cdot g)=g+A^{-1}d_{i_1}+A^{-2}d_{i_2}+\ldots \] for $i_j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $g\in\Z^n$. The image of the tile $\tile$ is the self-affine tile $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Taking $\phi=A^{-1}$ on $\Z^n$ with digit transversal $D$ realizes $\limGs[\Z^n]\cong\mathbb{R}^n$ with tile $\tile$ mapped onto $T$.

nodes.name: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ is the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^n$
nodes.statement: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs[\Z^n]$ is the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$.
conclusions: The push-forward $\Phi_*\mu$ of the measure $\mu$ on the limit $G$-space $\limGs[\Z^n]$ is the Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$

nodes.name: Lebesgue measure of a self-affine tile equals the measure number of the nucleus
nodes.statement: The Lebesgue measure of the self-affine tile $T$ is equal to the measure number $\mgr(\nucl)$ of the nucleus $\nucl$ of the associated self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$.
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda(T)=\mgr(\nucl)$, giving an algorithmic answer for the Lebesgue measure of an integral self-affine tile.
conclusions: The Lebesgue measure of the self-affine tile $T$ is equal to the measure number $\mgr(\nucl)$ of the nucleus $\nucl$ of the associated self-similar action $(\mathbb{Z}^n,X^{*})$

nodes.name: Relation to the graph $\mathcal{G}(\Z^n)$ of Gabardo and Yu
nodes.statement: The methods developed in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til} to find the Lebesgue measure of integral self-affine tiles are related to the discussion above. Take the complete automaton \cite[page~11]{self_sim_groups} of the self-similar action $(\Z^n,X^{*})$ (it actually coincides with the graph $B(\Z^n)$ from \cite{canon_numsys}), revert the direction of every edge, identify edges with the same starting and end vertices labeled by $(d_1,d_2)$ with the same difference $r=d_2-d_1$, and put the new label $r$ on this edge. We get the graph $\mathcal{G}(\Z^n)$ constructed in \cite{gab_yu:natur_til} and \cite{fract_numsys}. The set $W$ constructed using $\mathcal{G}(\Z^n)$ \cite[page~195]{gab_yu:natur_til} is precisely the nucleus $\nucl$. Hence the theory of self-similar groups provides a nice explanation to the ideas in \cite[Section~3]{gab_yu:natur_til} and the methods developed in Sections~2,4 can be seen as its non-abelian generalization.
nodes.statement_short: The Gabardo-Yu graph $\mathcal{G}(\Z^n)$ is a relabelled reversed complete automaton and their set $W$ is exactly the nucleus.

nodes.name: Does the tile always give a tiling with respect to a subgroup?
nodes.statement: It is shown in \cite{lag_wang:int_self_affine_II} that integral self-affine tile $T$ gives a lattice tiling of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with some lattice $L\subset\Z^n$. An interesting open question is whether this holds for any (self-replicating) contracting self-similar action $(G,X^{*})$ (or at least for self-similar actions of torsion-free nilpotent groups), i.e. the tile $\tile$ gives a tiling of $\limGs$ with some subgroup $H< G$.
nodes.statement_short: Is the lattice-tiling property of integral self-affine tiles valid for general contracting self-similar actions, with a subgroup $H<G$?

nodes.name: Heicklen-Hoffman: rational maps are $d$-adic Bernoulli
nodes.statement: Let $f(z)\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ be a rational map of the Riemann sphere $\Rs$ of degree $d\geq 2$. It is proved in \cite{invmeas_rat} that there exists a natural $f$-invariant probability measure $\mu_f$ with the support on the Julia set $J(f)$. In \cite{rational_bernoulli}, D.~Heicklen and C.~Hoffman showed that the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift, proving the conjecture in \cite{invmeas_rat,lub:entr_ration}.
nodes.statement_short: For a degree-$d$ rational map, $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugate to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift.
assumptions: Let $f(z)\in\mathbb{C}(z)$ be a rational map of the Riemann sphere $\Rs$ of degree $d\geq 2$
conclusions: there exists a natural $f$-invariant probability measure $\mu_f$ with the support on the Julia set $J(f)$
the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$ is conjugated to the one-sided Bernoulli $d$-shift

nodes.name: The limit dynamical system of $IMG(f)$ is conjugate to $(J(f),f)$
nodes.statement: The group $IMG(f)$ is contracting self-similar group and the limit dynamical system $(\lims[IMG(f)],\si)$ is conjugated to $(J(f),f)$ by Theorem~6.4.4 in \cite{self_sim_groups}.
conclusions: The group $IMG(f)$ is contracting self-similar group
the limit dynamical system $(\lims[IMG(f)],\si)$ is conjugated to $(J(f),f)$

nodes.name: The Bernoullicity theorem applies to $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$
nodes.statement: Under this conjugation the measure $\muls$ is send to the measure $\mu_f$, and we can apply Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} to the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$.
nodes.statement_short: The conjugacy carries $\muls$ to $\mu_f$, so the Bernoullicity theorem recovers Heicklen-Hoffman for sub-hyperbolic $f$.
conclusions: Under this conjugation the measure $\muls$ is send to the measure $\mu_f$
we can apply Theorem~\ref{theor_lims_conju_Bernoulli} to the dynamical system $(J(f),f,\mu_f)$

nodes.name: Proof of the integrality theorem for right-resolving graphs
nodes.statement: Let $w=\ldots x_2x_1\in\xmo$ and denote $w_n=x_n\ldots x_2x_1$ for $n\geq 1$. Observe, that $V(w)\subseteq V(w_n)$ and $V(w_n)\subseteq V(w_m)$ for $n\geq m$. Take a vertex $v\in \cap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n)$. Let $P_n$ be the set of all paths $e_n\ldots e_2e_1$ labeled by $w_n$ and ending in $v$. The set $P_n$ is a finite non-empty set for every $n$, and $e_{n-1}\ldots e_2e_1\in P_{n-1}$ for every path $e_n\ldots e_2e_1\in P_n$. Since the inverse limit of a sequence of finite non-empty sets is non-empty, there exists a left-infinite path $\ldots e_2e_1$ labeled by $w$ and ending in $v$. Then $v\in V(w)$ and we get \begin{equation} V(w)=\bigcap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n). \end{equation} From this follows that $|V(w)|=\min\limits_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ for $w\in\xmo$. Then \[ \min_{w\in\xmo} |V(w)|=\min_{w\in\xmo} \min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|=\min_{w\in X^*} |V(w)| \] and the second equality of the theorem is proved. Define the integer $k=\min_{w\in\xmo} |V(w)|$ and consider the set $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(\gr)\subseteq\xmo$ of all sequences $w\in\xmo$ such that $|V(w)|=k$. Define $\mathcal{O}^*$ as the set of finite words that satisfy the same condition. We have the following lemma. \begin{lemma} The set $\mathcal{O}$ is open and dense in $\xmo$, and $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. For each $w\in\mathcal{O}$ there is a beginning of $w$ that belongs to $\mathcal{O}^*$. Equivalently, $\mathcal{O}=\cup_{w\in\mathcal{O}^*}\xmo w$. \end{lemma} \begin{proof} If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that $|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in\xmo$. Hence $w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $\xmo w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus measurable. Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in\xmo$ contains the subword $u$ then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$. Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus $|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus $|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$. The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*, w'\in\xmo$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is dense in $\xmo$. \end{proof} By construction of the set $\mathcal{O}$ for every $w\in\mathcal{O}$ there exist exactly $k$ vertices $v$ such that $w\in F_v$. Let $\chi_{F_v}$ be the characteristic function of the set $F_v$. Then $\sum_{v\in V}\chi_{F_v}=k$ almost everywhere. Integrating we get $\mu_p(\gr)=\sum\limits_{v\in V} \mu_p(F_v)=k$.
nodes.statement_short: Inverse-limit compactness gives $V(w)=\cap_n V(w_n)$, so the minimum $k$ is attained on a full-measure set $\mathcal{O}$; integrating $\sum_v\chi_{F_v}=k$ yields $\mu_p(\gr)=k$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the vertex sets $V(w_n)$
nodes.statement: Let $w=\ldots x_2x_1\in\xmo$ and denote $w_n=x_n\ldots x_2x_1$ for $n\geq 1$. Observe, that $V(w)\subseteq V(w_n)$ and $V(w_n)\subseteq V(w_m)$ for $n\geq m$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up prefixes $w_n$ and note the nested inclusions of the vertex sets.

nodes.name: Inverse limit argument giving $V(w)=\cap_n V(w_n)$
nodes.statement: Take a vertex $v\in \cap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n)$. Let $P_n$ be the set of all paths $e_n\ldots e_2e_1$ labeled by $w_n$ and ending in $v$. The set $P_n$ is a finite non-empty set for every $n$, and $e_{n-1}\ldots e_2e_1\in P_{n-1}$ for every path $e_n\ldots e_2e_1\in P_n$. Since the inverse limit of a sequence of finite non-empty sets is non-empty, there exists a left-infinite path $\ldots e_2e_1$ labeled by $w$ and ending in $v$. Then $v\in V(w)$ and we get \begin{equation} V(w)=\bigcap_{n\geq 1} V(w_n). \end{equation} From this follows that $|V(w)|=\min\limits_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ for $w\in\xmo$. Then \[ \min_{w\in\xmo} |V(w)|=\min_{w\in\xmo} \min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|=\min_{w\in X^*} |V(w)| \] and the second equality of the theorem is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Non-emptiness of inverse limits of finite sets gives $V(w)=\cap_n V(w_n)$ and the second equality of the theorem.

nodes.name: Introduce the minimum $k$ and the set $\mathcal{O}$
nodes.statement: Define the integer $k=\min_{w\in\xmo} |V(w)|$ and consider the set $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}(\gr)\subseteq\xmo$ of all sequences $w\in\xmo$ such that $|V(w)|=k$. Define $\mathcal{O}^*$ as the set of finite words that satisfy the same condition. We have the following lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $k$ and the set $\mathcal{O}$ of sequences attaining it, then invoke the auxiliary lemma.

nodes.name: Integrate the multiplicity function to conclude
nodes.statement: By construction of the set $\mathcal{O}$ for every $w\in\mathcal{O}$ there exist exactly $k$ vertices $v$ such that $w\in F_v$. Let $\chi_{F_v}$ be the characteristic function of the set $F_v$. Then $\sum_{v\in V}\chi_{F_v}=k$ almost everywhere. Integrating we get $\mu_p(\gr)=\sum\limits_{v\in V} \mu_p(F_v)=k$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate $\sum_v\chi_{F_v}=k$ a.e. to get $\mu_p(\gr)=k$.

nodes.name: Proof that $\mathcal{O}$ is open, dense and of full measure
nodes.statement: If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that $|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in\xmo$. Hence $w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $\xmo w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus measurable. Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in\xmo$ contains the subword $u$ then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$. Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus $|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus $|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$. The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*, w'\in\xmo$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is dense in $\xmo$.
nodes.statement_short: Openness from a witnessing finite prefix; then right-resolvingness makes $|V|$ non-increasing under suffixes, so containing a minimizing subword suffices - and that happens almost surely.

nodes.name: Openness of $\mathcal{O}$ via a witnessing prefix
nodes.statement: If $w\in\mathcal{O}$ then $k=|V(w)|=\min_{n\geq 1} |V(w_n)|$ and there exists $N\geq 1$ such that $|V(w_N)|=k$. Then $k\leq |V(\omega w_N)|\leq |V(w_N)|=k$ for all $\omega\in\xmo$. Hence $w_N\in\mathcal{O}^*$, $\xmo w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$ and so $\mathcal{O}$ is open, and thus measurable.
nodes.statement_short: A prefix $w_N$ already attaining $k$ shows $\xmo w_N\subseteq\mathcal{O}$, so $\mathcal{O}$ is open.

nodes.name: Full measure and density via minimizing subwords
nodes.statement: Let $u\in X^*$ be such that $|V(u)|=k$. Let us show that if $w\in\xmo$ contains the subword $u$ then $w\in\mathcal{O}$. If $w=w'u$ then $k\leq |V(w'u)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and $w\in\mathcal{O}$. Observe that $V(ux)$ is the set of those vertices $v\in V$ for which there exists an edge labeled by $x$ which starts in some vertex of $V(u)$ and ends in $v$. Since the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving there is no more than one such an edge for each vertex of $V(u)$, and thus $|V(ux)|\leq |V(u)|$. It implies that if $w=w'uu'$ than $k\leq |V(w)|\leq |V(u)|=k$ and thus $|V(w)|=k$, so $w\in\mathcal{O}$. The Bernoulli measure of the set of all words $w'uu', u'\in X^*, w'\in\xmo$, is equal to $1$. Thus $\mu_p(\mathcal{O})=1$. It follows also that $\mathcal{O}$ is dense in $\xmo$.
nodes.statement_short: Right-resolvingness gives $|V(ux)|\leq|V(u)|$, so any sequence containing a minimizing subword lies in $\mathcal{O}$; such sequences have measure $1$.

nodes.name: Proof that $\B=\xo$ iff $\F=\xmo$
nodes.statement: Since the inverse limit of nonempty finite sets is nonempty, $\B=\xo$ ($\F=\xmo$) is equivalent to the fact that every finite word $v\in{X^*}$ labels some path in $\gr$.
nodes.statement_short: Both conditions are equivalent to every finite word labelling some path, by non-emptiness of inverse limits of finite sets.

nodes.name: Proof of the eigenvector characterization of $\vec\mu_p(\B)$ and $\vec\mu_p(\F)$
nodes.statement: By construction, for every vertex $v\in V$ we have \[ B_v=\bigsqcup_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} xB_u \] (here the union is disjoint because the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving). It implies \[ \mu_p(B_v)=\sum_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} p_x\mu_p(B_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{vu}\mu_p(B_{u}). \] Thus the nonzero vector $\vec \mu_p(\B)$ is the right eigenvector of $T_p$ for the eigenvalue~$1$. Similarly, \[ F_v=\bigcup_{u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v} F_{u}x,\ v\in V, \] and, since the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving, that implies \begin{equation*} \mu_p(F_v)\leq\sum_{u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v} p_x\mu_p(F_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{uv}\mu_p(F_{u})\quad \Rightarrow\quad \vec \mu_p(\F)\leq\vec \mu_p(\F) T_p. \end{equation*} The standard arguments based on the theory of nonnegative matrices (see for example \cite[proof of Theorem 4.5]{he_hui:self_affine}, \cite[p. 197]{gab_yu:natur_til}, \cite{handbook:rothblum}) end the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Disjoint decompositions of $B_v$ and $F_v$ turn the measure vectors into (in)equalities $\vec\mu=T_p\vec\mu$, and nonnegative-matrix theory upgrades the $\F$-inequality to equality.

nodes.name: Disjoint decomposition of $B_v$ gives a right eigenvector
nodes.statement: By construction, for every vertex $v\in V$ we have \[ B_v=\bigsqcup_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} xB_u \] (here the union is disjoint because the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving). It implies \[ \mu_p(B_v)=\sum_{v\stackrel{x}\rightarrow u} p_x\mu_p(B_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{vu}\mu_p(B_{u}). \] Thus the nonzero vector $\vec \mu_p(\B)$ is the right eigenvector of $T_p$ for the eigenvalue~$1$.
nodes.statement_short: Right-resolvingness makes the decomposition of $B_v$ disjoint, so $\vec\mu_p(\B)=T_p\vec\mu_p(\B)$.

nodes.name: Decomposition of $F_v$ gives the inequality $\vec\mu_p(\F)\leq\vec\mu_p(\F)T_p$
nodes.statement: Similarly, \[ F_v=\bigcup_{u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v} F_{u}x,\ v\in V, \] and, since the graph $\gr$ is right-resolving, that implies \begin{equation*} \mu_p(F_v)\leq\sum_{u\stackrel{x}\rightarrow v} p_x\mu_p(F_{u})=\sum_{u\in V} t_{uv}\mu_p(F_{u})\quad \Rightarrow\quad \vec \mu_p(\F)\leq\vec \mu_p(\F) T_p. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: The (possibly overlapping) decomposition of $F_v$ only yields the subinvariance $\vec\mu_p(\F)\leq\vec\mu_p(\F)T_p$.

nodes.name: Nonnegative-matrix theory finishes the argument
nodes.statement: The standard arguments based on the theory of nonnegative matrices (see for example \cite[proof of Theorem 4.5]{he_hui:self_affine}, \cite[p. 197]{gab_yu:natur_til}, \cite{handbook:rothblum}) end the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Invoke Perron-Frobenius-type facts for nonnegative matrices to conclude equality.

nodes.name: Proof of the properties of the measures of tiles
nodes.statement: Let us show that $\mu(A)\geq |X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$ for any Borel set $A$. Consider sequences which represent points of the sets $A$ and $\tau_x(A)$: \[ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(A)=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g\cdot g \ \ \Rightarrow \ \ \pi^{-1}_{\limGs[]}(\tau_x(A))=\bigcup_{g\in G}T_g g(x)\cdot g|_x. \] It implies \[ \mu(\tau_x(A))\leq \sum_{g\in G} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu_u (T_g)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu(A). \] By applying this inequality $n$ times we get $|X|^n\mu(\tile_v)=|X|^n\mu(\tau_v(\tile))\leq\mu(\tile)$ for $v\in{X}^n$. Since $\tile=\cup_{u\in X^n}\tile_{u}$ we have that \[ \mu(\tile)\leq\sum_{u\in X^n}\mu(\tile_{u})\leq\sum_{u\in X^n}\frac{1}{|X|^n}\mu(\tile)=\mu(\tile). \] Hence all the above inequalities are actually equalities, $\mu(\tile)=|X|^n\mu(\tile_{u})$ for every $u\in X^n$, and $\mu(\tile_u\cap\tile_{u'})=0$ for different $u,u'\in X^n$. Notice that since every Borel set $A\subset\tile$ can be approximated by unions of tiles of the same level and using items 1 and 2 we have that if $\mu(\tau_x(A))<\varepsilon$ then $\mu(A)<\varepsilon|X|$. It is left to prove item 3. First, let us show that the assertion holds for the tiles $\tile_v$. Since the measure $\mu|_{\tile}$ is concentrated on the tile $\tile$, up to sets of measure zero the set $\tau_x^{-1}(\tile_v)$ is equal $\tile_u$ if $v=ux$, and is empty if the last letter of $v$ is not $x$. Really, if $t\in\tau_x^{-1}(\tile_{ux})$ and $t\in\tile_v$ with $v\neq u, |v|=|u|$, then $\tau_x(t)\in\tile_{vx}\cap\tile_{ux}$ and the measure of such points is zero. Hence \[ \mu|_{\tile}(\tile_v)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\tile}(\tile_u)=\sum_{x\in X} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\tile}(\tau_x^{-1}(\tile_v)). \] Now we can approximate any Borel set by unions of tiles and pass to the limit.
nodes.statement_short: Prove $\mu(A)\geq|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$, iterate it to squeeze all inequalities into equalities (items 1 and 2), then verify self-similarity on tiles and approximate Borel sets.

nodes.name: The contraction inequality $\mu(A)\geq|X|\mu(\tau_x(A))$

nodes.statement_short: The sandwich $\mu(\tile)\leq\sum_u\mu(\tile_u)\leq\mu(\tile)$ forces equalities, giving items 1 and 2.

nodes.statement: Notice that since every Borel set $A\subset\tile$ can be approximated by unions of tiles of the same level and using items 1 and 2 we have that if $\mu(\tau_x(A))<\varepsilon$ then $\mu(A)<\varepsilon|X|$.

Since the measure $\mu|_{\tile}$ is concentrated on the tile $\tile$, up to sets of measure zero the set $\tau_x^{-1}(\tile_v)$ is equal $\tile_u$ if $v=ux$, and is empty if the last letter of $v$ is not $x$. Hence \[ \mu|_{\tile}(\tile_v)=\frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\tile}(\tile_u)=\sum_{x\in X} \frac{1}{|X|}\mu|_{\tile}(\tau_x^{-1}(\tile_v)). \] Now we can approximate any Borel set by unions of tiles and pass to the limit.

nodes.name: Proof that the boundary of the tile is null
nodes.statement: Take $x\in\partial\tile$. Suppose that $x$ is covered by exactly $k=\mu(\tile)$ tiles. Let $U\subset\dot{\limGs}$ be the neighborhood of $x$ which intersects with finitely many tiles, say with $l\geq k$ tiles. By subtracting any tile that does not contain $x$ we may suppose that $l=k$, that is, $U$ has nonempty intersection only with those tiles that contain $x$. Now, since $x$ is in the boundary of $\tile$, there is a point $x'$ in $U$ that is not covered by $\tile$ (otherwise $x\in U\subset\tile$), thus $x'$ is covered by less than $k$ tiles, contradiction. Hence $\partial\tile$ is in the complement of $\dot{\limGs}$ and has measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: a boundary point of exact multiplicity $k$ would force a nearby point of multiplicity $<k$, so $\partial\tile\subset\limGs\setminus\dot{\limGs}$.

nodes.name: Contradiction setup: a boundary point of exact multiplicity
nodes.statement: Take $x\in\partial\tile$. Suppose that $x$ is covered by exactly $k=\mu(\tile)$ tiles. Let $U\subset\dot{\limGs}$ be the neighborhood of $x$ which intersects with finitely many tiles, say with $l\geq k$ tiles. By subtracting any tile that does not contain $x$ we may suppose that $l=k$, that is, $U$ has nonempty intersection only with those tiles that contain $x$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $x\in\partial\tile$ has exact multiplicity $k$ and shrink a neighbourhood to meet only the $k$ tiles through $x$.

nodes.name: Derive the contradiction and conclude
nodes.statement: Now, since $x$ is in the boundary of $\tile$, there is a point $x'$ in $U$ that is not covered by $\tile$ (otherwise $x\in U\subset\tile$), thus $x'$ is covered by less than $k$ tiles, contradiction. Hence $\partial\tile$ is in the complement of $\dot{\limGs}$ and has measure $0$.
nodes.statement_short: A nearby point missed by $\tile$ has multiplicity $<k$, contradicting $U\subset\dot{\limGs}$.

nodes.name: Proof that $\alpha$ preserves measure
nodes.statement:
Let $
ucl$ be the nucleus and $	ile$ be the tile of the action $(G,X^{*})$. By Theorem~ef{theor_tile_measure} and Theorem~ef{theor_measure_graph_integer}  egin{equation} \mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile)=\mgr(\gr_
ucl)=\min_{w\in\xmo} |V(w)|=k\in\mathbb{N}, \end{equation} where $V(w)$ is defined using the graph $\gr_
ucl$. Consider \[ \pi_Y^{-1}(\alpha(	ile))= igcup_{g\in G} T_g\cdot g\quad (\mbox{here } T_g\subseteq Y^{-\omega}), \] where $\pi_Y:Y^{-\omega}	imes Gightarrow \limGs$ is the canonical projection. Take $w\in Y^{-\omega}$ and let us prove that there exist at least $k$ elements $g\in G$ such that $w\in T_g$. The tiles $	ile\cdot g$ cover the limit $G$-space $\limGs[(G,X^*)]$, and we can find $g\in G$ such that if $x=\alpha^{-1}(y)$ for $y=\pi_{Y}(w\cdot g)\in\limGs[(G,Y^*)]$ then $x$ belongs to the tile $	ile$. Then $x$ is represented by the sequence $u\cdot 1$ for $u\in\xmo$. Equation~(ef{eqn_theor_meraXY_mu tile }) implies $|V(u)|\geq k$ and so there exist $k$ elements $h_1,\ldots, h_k\in
ucl$ and sequences $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in\xmo$ such that for every $i$ there exists a left-infinite path in the nucleus $
ucl$ which ends in $h_i$ and is labeled by $(u,u_i)$. By Proposition~ef{prop_asympt_Moore_diagr} \[ x=\pi_X(u\cdot 1)=\pi_X(u_i\cdot h_i)\quad\mbox{ and }\quad x\cdot h_i^{-1}\in	ile \] for every $i=1,\ldots, k$. Then \[ \pi_Y(w\cdot gh_i^{-1})=\pi_Y(w\cdot g)h_i^{-1}=y\cdot h_i^{-1}=\alpha(x\cdot h_i^{-1})\in\alpha(	ile) \] and thus $w\in T_{gh_i^{-1}}$ for all $i=1,\ldots, k$. Let $\chi_{T_g}$ be the characteristic function of the set $T_g$. Then $\sum_{g\in G}\chi_{T_g}(x)\geq k$ for almost all $x$. Integrating we get $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(	ile))=\sum_{g\in G} \mu_u(T_g)\geq k=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile)$. Let us now show that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(	ile_v))\leq\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile_v)$ for any $v\in X^*$. Indeed, let $n=|v|$, then it follows from Theorem ef{theor_limsX hom limsY} that $\alpha(	ile_v)=\alpha(	au_v(	ile))=	au_u(\alpha(	ile))g$ for some word $u\in Y^n$ and $g\in G$. Thus  egin{eqnarray*} \mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(	ile_v))&=&\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(	au_u(\alpha(	ile)))\leq rac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(	ile))=\ &=& rac{1}{|X|^n}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile)=\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile_v). \end{eqnarray*} Let us prove that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$. Indeed, let $\mu_{(G,X^*)}(A)<\varepsilon$, $\pi^{-1}_{X}(A)=\cup_g T_g\cdot g$. Then $\sum_g\mu_u(T_g)<\varepsilon$. It follows that there exist $v_{i,g}\in X^*$ such that $T_g\subset\cup_i\xmo v_{i,g}$ and $\sum_{i,g}|X|^{-|v_{i,g}|}<\varepsilon$. Then $A\subset\cup_{i,g}	ile_{v_{i,g}}\cdot g$, and we have that $\sum_{i,g}\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile)$. Then $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(A))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,Y^*)}(\alpha(	ile_{v_{i,g}}))\leq\sum\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile_{v_{i,g}})<\varepsilon\mu_{(G,X^*)}(	ile)$. Since $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary, we are done. We will now prove that $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha\leq\mu_{(G,X^*)}$. Since both $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ and $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$ are invariant under multiplication by $g\in G$ it suffices to prove this inequality for sets $A\subset	ile$. Since any Borel $A$ is a union of a closed set and a set of arbitrarily small measure, it suffices to prove the inequality for closed sets, as $\mu_{(G,Y^*)}\circ\alpha$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu_{(G,X^*)}$ by above. So let $A\subset	ile$ be a closed set. For each $n$, let $A_n$ be the union of all tiles $	ile_v,v\in X^n,$ that have non-empty intersection with $A$. Let us show that $A=\cap_n A_n$. Suppose $x\in\cap A_n$, and $x$ is not in $A$. Then for each $n$ there is $v_n\in X^n$ such that $	ile_{v_n}$ has nonempty intersection with $A$ and $x\in	ile_{v_n}$. It follows that $x$ has some representation $u_nv_n\in\xmo$. Since the number of such representations is finite, we may choose subsequence $n_k$ such that $v_{n_k}$ is the beginning of some word $v\in\xmo$. Since $A$ is compact it follows that $A$ has nonempty intersection with $\cap_k	ile_{v_{n_k}}$, thus $\cap_k	ile_{v_{n_k}}$ contains at least two points, which is impossible. Since $A_n$ is the union of some tiles of level $n$, which are disjoint up to sets of measure $0$, the inequality also holds for all $A_n$. Going to the limit, we get the inequality for $A$. By interchanging $X$ and $Y$ we get the reverse inequality, and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided squeeze: multiplicity counting gives $\mu_Y(\alpha(\tile))\geq k$, tile scaling plus absolute continuity gives $\mu_Y\circ\alpha\leq\mu_X$, and swapping $X$ and $Y$ closes the argument.
